sanskrit: tasmin hate mahāsattve maheṣvāse mahābale mahārathe naravyāghre kim u āsīn manas tadā
english: When that great-souled one was slain — the mighty archer, vast in strength, the great chariot-warrior, the tiger among men — what then, tell me, was the temper of their minds?

sanskrit: ārtiḥ parā māviśati yataḥ śaṃsasi me hatam kurūṇām ṛṣabhaṃ vīram akampyaṃ puruṣarṣabham
english: A boundless anguish enters me, since you tell me he is slain — the bull of the Kurus, the unshakable hero, that bull among men.

sanskrit: ke taṃ yāntam anupreyuḥ ke cāsyāsan purogamāḥ ke 'tiṣṭhan ke nyavartanta ke 'bhyavartanta saṃjaya
english: Who followed after him as he advanced, and who went before him? Who held their ground, who turned back, and who pressed onward, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: ke śūrā rathaśārdūlam acyutaṃ kṣatriyarṣabham rathānīkaṃ gāhamānaṃ sahasā pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ
english: What heroes followed close behind that tiger among chariot-warriors, the unfaltering one, the bull among kṣatriyas, as he plunged headlong into the host of chariots?

sanskrit: yas tamo 'rka ivāpohan parasainyam amitrahā sahasraraśmipratimaḥ pareṣāṃ bhayam ādadhat akarod duṣkaraṃ karma raṇe kauravaśāsanāt
english: He who, like the sun dispelling darkness, that slayer of foes scattered the enemy host — like one of a thousand rays — and struck terror into his adversaries, performing in battle a deed hard to do, at the command of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: grasamānam anīkāni ya enaṃ paryavārayan kṛtinaṃ taṃ durādharṣaṃ samyag yāsyantam antike kathaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ yuddhe pāṇḍavāḥ pratyavārayan
english: As he was devouring whole armies, who hemmed him in close at hand — that accomplished and unassailable warrior, advancing straight upon them? How did the Pāṇḍavas hold back the son of Śaṃtanu in the fight?

sanskrit: nikṛntantam anīkāni śaradaṃṣṭraṃ tarasvinam cāpavyāttānanaṃ ghoram asijihvaṃ durāsadam
english: He who hewed down the armies, swift, his fangs of arrows, his mouth gaping wide as a bow, terrible, his tongue a sword, unapproachable —

sanskrit: atyanyān puruṣavyāghrān hrīmantam aparājitam pātayām āsa kaunteyaḥ kathaṃ tam ajitaṃ yudhi
english: He who surpassed all other tigers among men, modest and unconquered — how did the son of Kuntī bring down that one who had never been vanquished in battle?

sanskrit: ugradhanvānam ugreṣuṃ vartamānaṃ rathottame pareṣām uttamāṅgāni pracinvantaṃ śiteṣubhiḥ
english: With his fierce bow and fierce shafts, standing upon his peerless chariot, harvesting the heads of his foes with whetted arrows —

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ mahat sainyaṃ yaṃ dṛṣṭvodyantam āhave kālāgnim iva durdharṣaṃ samaveṣṭata nityaśaḥ
english: He whom the great host of the Pāṇḍavas, beholding him rise up in the fray unassailable like the fire of doom, encircled again and again —

sanskrit: parikṛṣya sa senāṃ me daśarātram anīkahā jagāmāstam ivādityaḥ kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
english: For ten nights that destroyer of armies harrowed my host, and then, like the sun, he set, having wrought a deed most hard to do.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa śakra ivākṣayyaṃ varṣaṃ śaramayaṃ sṛjan jaghāna yudhi yodhānām arbudaṃ daśabhir dinaiḥ
english: He who, like Śakra, loosed an unfailing rain made of arrows, and in ten days slew a hundred million of the warriors in battle —

sanskrit: sa śete niṣṭanan bhūmau vātarugṇa iva drumaḥ mama durmantritenāsau yathā nārhaḥ sa bhārataḥ
english: He now lies groaning upon the earth like a tree shattered by the wind — that descendant of Bharata, who deserved no such fate, brought low by my evil counsel.

sanskrit: kathaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānām anīkinī prahartum aśakat tatra bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: How was the army of the Pāṇḍavas able, beholding the son of Śaṃtanu there, to strike at Bhīṣma of terrible prowess?

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhīṣmeṇa saṃgrāmam akurvan pāṇḍunandanāḥ kathaṃ ca nājayad bhīṣmo droṇe jīvati saṃjaya
english: How did the sons of Pāṇḍu wage war against Bhīṣma, and how did Bhīṣma fail to conquer while Droṇa yet lived, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: kṛpe saṃnihite tatra bharadvājātmaje tathā bhīṣmaḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kathaṃ sa nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: With Kṛpa close at hand there, and the son of Bharadvāja as well, how did Bhīṣma, the best of those who strike, come to his death?

sanskrit: kathaṃ cātirathas tena pāñcālyena śikhaṇḍinā bhīṣmo vinihato yuddhe devair api durutsahaḥ
english: And how was that supreme chariot-warrior Bhīṣma — hard for even the gods to withstand — slain in battle by the Pāñcāla, Śikhaṇḍin?

sanskrit: yaḥ spardhate raṇe nityaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahābalam ajitaṃ jāmadagnyena śakratulyaparākramam
english: He who in battle ever rivaled the mighty son of Jamadagni, unvanquished by that son of Jamadagni, his valor the equal of Śakra's —

sanskrit: taṃ hataṃ samare bhīṣmaṃ mahārathabalocitam saṃjayācakṣva me vīraṃ yena śarma na vidmahe
english: Tell me, Saṃjaya, of that hero Bhīṣma, slain in the fight, worthy of the strength of the greatest chariot-warriors — he without whom we know no refuge.

sanskrit: māmakāḥ ke maheṣvāsā nājahuḥ saṃjayācyutam duryodhanasamādiṣṭāḥ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: Which of my mighty archers did not abandon that unfaltering one, Saṃjaya? Which heroes, charged by Duryodhana, encircled him to guard him?

sanskrit: yac chikhaṇḍimukhāḥ sarve pāṇḍavā bhīṣmam abhyayuḥ kaccin na kuravo bhītās tatyajuḥ saṃjayācyutam
english: When all the Pāṇḍavas, with Śikhaṇḍin at their head, advanced upon Bhīṣma, did the Kurus not, in their fear, abandon that unfaltering one, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: maurvīghoṣastanayitnuḥ pṛṣatkapṛṣato mahān dhanurhvādamahāśabdo mahāmegha ivonnataḥ
english: With the twang of his bowstring for thunder, his arrows for a dappling of raindrops, the great roar of his bow for its mighty voice — towering like a vast storm-cloud —

sanskrit: yad abhyavarṣat kaunteyān sapāñcālān sasṛñjayān nighnan pararathān vīro dānavān iva vajrabhṛt
english: As he rained down upon the sons of Kuntī with the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas, that hero smiting the enemy chariots like the wielder of the thunderbolt smiting the Dānavas —

sanskrit: iṣvastrasāgaraṃ ghoraṃ bāṇagrāhaṃ durāsadam kārmukormiṇam akṣayyam advīpaṃ samare 'plavam gadāsimakarāvartaṃ hayagrāhaṃ gajākulam
english: A dreadful ocean of arrows and missiles, with shafts for its sea-monsters, unapproachable, its waves the bows, inexhaustible, in battle without an isle and without a raft, its whirlpools the maces and swords, its crocodiles the horses, its waters thronged with elephants —

sanskrit: hayān gajān padātāṃś ca rathāṃś ca tarasā bahūn nimajjayantaṃ samare paravīrāpahāriṇam
english: He who swiftly drowned horses, elephants, foot-soldiers, and chariots in throngs upon the field, that carrier-off of the enemy's heroes —

sanskrit: vidahyamānaṃ kopena tejasā ca paraṃtapam veleva makarāvāsaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: That scorcher of foes, blazing with wrath and with splendor — what heroes encircled him as a shore holds back the home of sea-monsters?

sanskrit: bhīṣmo yad akarot karma samare saṃjayārihā duryodhanahitārthāya ke tadāsya puro 'bhavan
english: When Bhīṣma, that slayer of foes, did his deed in battle for Duryodhana's sake, Saṃjaya — who were they that stood before him then?

sanskrit: ke 'rakṣan dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ bhīṣmasyāmitatejasaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ ke parān vīrā upāsedhan yatavratāḥ
english: Who guarded the right wheel of Bhīṣma of measureless splendor? What heroes, steadfast in their vows, held off the foe from behind?

sanskrit: ke purastād avartanta rakṣanto bhīṣmam antike ke 'rakṣann uttaraṃ cakraṃ vīrā vīrasya yudhyataḥ
english: Who took their station in front, guarding Bhīṣma close at hand? What heroes guarded the left wheel of the hero as he fought?

sanskrit: vāme cakre vartamānāḥ ke 'ghnan saṃjaya sṛñjayān sametāgram anīkeṣu ke 'bhyarakṣan durāsadam
english: Stationed at the left wheel, who slew the Sṛñjayas, Saṃjaya? Who, gathered at the forefront of the ranks, guarded that unassailable one?

sanskrit: pārśvataḥ ke 'bhyavartanta gacchanto durgamāṃ gatim samūhe ke parān vīrān pratyayudhyanta saṃjaya
english: Who pressed forward at his flanks, following a path hard to tread? Amid the throng, who did battle against the heroes of the foe, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇaḥ kathaṃ vīrair gopyamānāś ca tena te durjayānām anīkāni nājayaṃs tarasā yudhi
english: If he was guarded by heroes, and they in turn were sheltered by him, how did the armies of those hard to conquer not swiftly prevail in the fight?

sanskrit: sarvalokeśvarasyeva parameṣṭhiprajāpateḥ kathaṃ prahartum api te śekuḥ saṃjaya pāṇḍavāḥ
english: As though against the lord of all worlds, the supreme Prajāpati — how were the Pāṇḍavas even able to strike at him, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: yasmin dvīpe samāśritya yudhyanti kuravaḥ paraiḥ taṃ nimagnaṃ naravyāghraṃ bhīṣmaṃ śaṃsasi saṃjaya
english: The island upon which the Kurus relied as they fought their foes — that tiger among men, Bhīṣma, now sunk beneath the waters, you tell me is fallen, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: yasya vīrye samāśvasya mama putro bṛhadbalaḥ na pāṇḍavān agaṇayat kathaṃ sa nihataḥ paraiḥ
english: In whose valor my son, mighty in strength, set his trust and reckoned the Pāṇḍavas as nothing — how was he slain by the foe?

sanskrit: yaḥ purā vibudhaiḥ sendraiḥ sāhāyye yuddhadurmadaḥ kāṅkṣito dānavān ghnadbhiḥ pitā mama mahāvrataḥ
english: He who long ago, frenzied for war, was sought as an ally by the gods with Indra at their head when they smote the Dānavas — my father, great in his vow —

sanskrit: yasmiñ jāte mahāvīrye śaṃtanur lokaśaṃkare śokaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca dainyaṃ ca prājahāt putralakṣmaṇi
english: At whose birth Śaṃtanu, in that son of mighty valor, blessing to the world and his father's pride, cast off sorrow, grief, and despair —

sanskrit: prajñā parāyaṇaṃ tajjñaṃ saddharmanirataṃ śucim vedavedāṅgatattvajñaṃ kathaṃ śaṃsasi me hatam
english: That refuge of wisdom, knower of it, devoted to the true law, pure, versed in the truth of the Vedas and their auxiliaries — how do you tell me he is slain?

sanskrit: sarvāstravinayopetaṃ dāntaṃ śāntaṃ manasvinam hataṃ śāṃtanavaṃ śrutvā manye śeṣaṃ balaṃ hatam
english: Endowed with the discipline of every weapon, self-controlled, serene, high-minded — hearing that the son of Śaṃtanu is slain, I deem the rest of my army slain as well.

sanskrit: dharmād adharmo balavān saṃprāpta iti me matiḥ yatra vṛddhaṃ guruṃ hatvā rājyam icchanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Unrighteousness has grown stronger than righteousness — such is my judgment — where the Pāṇḍavas, having slain their aged elder, still desire the kingdom.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyaḥ purā rāmaḥ sarvāstravid anuttamaḥ ambārtham udyataḥ saṃkhye bhīṣmeṇa yudhi nirjitaḥ
english: Long ago Rāma, son of Jamadagni, knower of every weapon, unsurpassed, took up arms in the cause of Ambā and in the battle was vanquished by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tam indrasamakarmāṇaṃ kakudaṃ sarvadhanvinām hataṃ śaṃsasi bhīṣmaṃ me kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param
english: That Bhīṣma, whose deeds were the equal of Indra's, the crest of all bowmen — you tell me he is slain. What grief can be greater than this?

sanskrit: asakṛt kṣatriyavrātāḥ saṃkhye yena vinirjitāḥ jāmadagnyas tathā rāmaḥ paravīranighātinā
english: He by whom hosts of kṣatriyas were again and again overcome in battle, and Rāma, son of Jamadagni, too — that slayer of the enemy's heroes —

sanskrit: tasmān nūnaṃ mahāvīryād bhārgavād yuddhadurmadāt tejovīryabalair bhūyāñ śikhaṇḍī drupadātmajaḥ
english: Surely, then, in splendor, valor, and strength, Śikhaṇḍin the son of Drupada was greater than that mighty descendant of Bhṛgu, frenzied for war.

sanskrit: yaḥ śūraṃ kṛtinaṃ yuddhe sarvaśāstraviśāradam paramāstravidaṃ vīraṃ jaghāna bharatarṣabham
english: He who slew that hero — valiant, accomplished in war, skilled in every science, master of the supreme weapons, that bull of the Bhāratas —

sanskrit: ke vīrās tam amitraghnam anvayuḥ śatrusaṃsadi śaṃsa me tad yathā vṛttaṃ yuddhaṃ bhīṣmasya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: What heroes followed that slayer of foes into the assembly of the enemy? Tell me how it came to pass — the battle of Bhīṣma with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yoṣeva hatavīrā me senā putrasya saṃjaya agopam iva codbhrāntaṃ gokulaṃ tad balaṃ mama
english: My son's army is like a woman whose hero is slain, Saṃjaya; that host of mine is like a herd of cattle scattered in panic, without a herdsman.

sanskrit: pauruṣaṃ sarvalokasya paraṃ yasya mahāhave parāsikte ca vas tasmin katham āsīn manas tadā
english: He whose manhood in the great battle surpassed that of all the world — when he was struck down, what then was the temper of your minds?

sanskrit: jīvite 'py adya sāmarthyaṃ kim ivāsmāsu saṃjaya ghātayitvā mahāvīryaṃ pitaraṃ lokadhārmikam
english: What strength is there in us even to live this day, Saṃjaya, having caused the death of that father of mighty valor, righteous before all the world?

sanskrit: agādhe salile magnāṃ nāvaṃ dṛṣṭveva pāragāḥ bhīṣme hate bhṛśaṃ duḥkhān manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Like men seeking the farther shore who see their boat foundering in fathomless water, my sons, I think, grieve sorely now that Bhīṣma is slain.

sanskrit: adrisāramayaṃ nūnaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama yac chrutvā puruṣavyāghraṃ hataṃ bhīṣmaṃ na dīryate
english: Surely my heart is made of the very substance of mountains, exceedingly hard, that, hearing the tiger among men, Bhīṣma, is slain, it does not burst asunder.

sanskrit: yasminn astraṃ ca medhā ca nītiś ca bharatarṣabhe aprameyāṇi durdharṣe kathaṃ sa nihato yudhi
english: In whom — that bull of the Bhāratas, unassailable — weaponry, wisdom, and statecraft were beyond all measure: how was he slain in battle?

sanskrit: na cāstreṇa na śauryeṇa tapasā medhayā na ca na dhṛtyā na punas tyāgān mṛtyoḥ kaś cid vimucyate
english: Not by weapon, not by valor, not by austerity nor by wisdom, not by steadfastness, nor again by renunciation — by none of these is any creature delivered from death.

sanskrit: kālo nūnaṃ mahāvīryaḥ sarvalokaduratyayaḥ yatra śāṃtanavaṃ bhīṣmaṃ hataṃ śaṃsasi saṃjaya
english: Surely Time is of mighty power, not to be overpassed by all the worlds, since you tell me that the son of Śaṃtanu, Bhīṣma, is slain, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtapto mahad duḥkham acintayan āśaṃse 'haṃ purā trāṇaṃ bhīṣmāc chaṃtanunandanāt
english: Consumed by grief for my sons, brooding on this great sorrow — once I had hoped for protection from Bhīṣma, the joy of Śaṃtanu.

sanskrit: yadādityam ivāpaśyat patitaṃ bhuvi saṃjaya duryodhanaḥ śāṃtanavaṃ kiṃ tadā pratyapadyata
english: When Duryodhana saw the son of Śaṃtanu fallen to the earth like the sun, Saṃjaya — what did he do then?

sanskrit: nāhaṃ sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ vā buddhyā saṃjaya cintayan śeṣaṃ kiṃ cit prapaśyāmi pratyanīke mahīkṣitām
english: Pondering with my mind, Saṃjaya, over my own and over the foe, I see nothing whatever remaining among the kings ranged against us.

sanskrit: dāruṇaḥ kṣatradharmo 'yam ṛṣibhiḥ saṃpradarśitaḥ yatra śāṃtanavaṃ hatvā rājyam icchanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Cruel is this duty of the kṣatriya, set forth by the seers, wherein the Pāṇḍavas, having slain the son of Śaṃtanu, still desire the kingdom.

sanskrit: vayaṃ vā rājyam icchāmo ghātayitvā pitāmaham kṣatradharme sthitāḥ pārthā nāparādhyanti putrakāḥ
english: Or it is we who desire the kingdom, having caused the grandsire's death; standing fast in the kṣatriya's duty, the sons of Pṛthā commit no wrong, my sons.

sanskrit: etad āryeṇa kartavyaṃ kṛcchrāsv āpatsu saṃjaya parākramaḥ paraṃ śaktyā tac ca tasmin pratiṣṭhitam
english: This is what a noble man must do in dire calamities, Saṃjaya: to strive valiantly with all his power — and in him that valor was firmly set.

sanskrit: anīkāni vinighnantaṃ hrīmantam aparājitam kathaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ tāta pāṇḍuputrā nyapātayan
english: As he was destroying the armies, modest and unconquered — how, dear one, did the sons of Pāṇḍu bring down the son of Śaṃtanu?

sanskrit: kathaṃ yuktāny anīkāni kathaṃ yuddhaṃ mahātmabhiḥ kathaṃ vā nihato bhīṣmaḥ pitā saṃjaya me paraiḥ
english: How were the armies arrayed, how did the great-souled ones do battle, and how was Bhīṣma, my father, slain by the foe, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca karṇaś ca śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ duḥśāsanaś ca kitavo hate bhīṣme kim abruvan
english: And Duryodhana, and Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala, and the cheat Duḥśāsana — when Bhīṣma was slain, what did they say?

sanskrit: yac charīrair upastīrṇāṃ naravāraṇavājinām śaraśaktigadākhaḍgatomarākṣāṃ bhayāvahām
english: That assembly strewn with the bodies of men, elephants, and horses, with arrows, spears, maces, swords, and javelins for its dice, dreadful to behold —

sanskrit: prāviśan kitavā mandāḥ sabhāṃ yudhi durāsadām prāṇadyūte pratibhaye ke 'dīvyanta nararṣabhāḥ
english: The foolish gamblers entered that hall of battle, hard to enter — in that fearful game played for life itself, which bulls among men cast the dice?

sanskrit: ke 'jayan ke jitās tatra hṛtalakṣā nipātitāḥ anye bhīṣmāc chāṃtanavāt tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Who won there and who were defeated, their stakes lost, struck down — besides Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: na hi me śāntir astīha yudhi devavrataṃ hatam pitaraṃ bhīmakarmāṇaṃ śrutvā me duḥkham āviśat
english: There is no peace for me here; hearing that Devavrata, my father of terrible deeds, has been slain in battle, sorrow has entered into me.

sanskrit: ārtiṃ me hṛdaye rūḍhāṃ mahatīṃ putrakāritām tvaṃ siñcan sarpiṣevāgnim uddīpayasi saṃjaya
english: The great anguish rooted in my heart, brought on by my sons — you inflame it as one pouring clarified butter inflames a fire, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: mahāntaṃ bhāram udyamya viśrutaṃ sārvalaukikam dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ bhīṣmaṃ manye śocanti putrakāḥ
english: Beholding Bhīṣma slain — who had taken up that great burden, renowned throughout all the worlds — my sons, I think, now grieve.

sanskrit: śroṣyāmi tāni duḥkhāni duryodhanakṛtāny aham tasmān me sarvam ācakṣva yad vṛttaṃ tatra saṃjaya
english: I shall hear all those sorrows wrought by Duryodhana; therefore tell me everything that came to pass there, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃgrāme pṛthivīśānāṃ mandasyābuddhisaṃbhavam apanītaṃ sunītaṃ vā tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: In the battle of the lords of the earth, whatever sprang from the folly of that dullard, whether ill-counselled or well-counselled — tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: yat kṛtaṃ tatra bhīṣmeṇa saṃgrāme jayam icchatā tejoyuktaṃ kṛtāstreṇa śaṃsa tac cāpy aśeṣataḥ
english: What was done there by Bhīṣma in the battle as he sought victory — full of splendor, accomplished in arms — tell me that too, leaving nothing out.

sanskrit: yathā tad abhavad yuddhaṃ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ krameṇa yena yasmiṃś ca kāle yac ca yathā ca tat
english: How that battle of the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas came to be — in what sequence, at what time, what happened and in what manner — tell it all.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tvadyukto 'yam anupraśno mahārāja yathārhasi na tu duryodhane doṣam imam āsaktum arhasi
english: Saṃjaya said: This question is worthy of you, great king, as befits you; yet you ought not to lay this blame upon Duryodhana.

sanskrit: ya ātmano duścaritād aśubhaṃ prāpnuyān naraḥ enasā tena nānyaṃ sa upāśaṅkitum arhati
english: The man who through his own ill conduct meets with misfortune ought not to lay the guilt of that sin upon another.

sanskrit: mahārāja manuṣyeṣu nindyaṃ yaḥ sarvam ācaret sa vadhyaḥ sarvalokasya ninditāni samācaran
english: Great king, the man who commits among men every blameworthy deed deserves to be slain by all the world, doing as he does what is condemned.

sanskrit: nikāro nikṛtiprajñaiḥ pāṇḍavais tvatpratīkṣayā anubhūtaḥ sahāmātyaiḥ kṣāntaṃ ca suciraṃ vane
english: Insult was endured by the Pāṇḍavas, deep in cunning, out of deference to you, together with their counsellors; and long indeed did they bear it patiently in the forest.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ ca gajānāṃ ca śūrāṇāṃ cāmitaujasām pratyakṣaṃ yan mayā dṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yogabalena ca
english: What I have seen with my own eyes of the horses, the elephants, and the heroes of measureless might, and what I have seen by the power of yoga —

sanskrit: śṛṇu tat pṛthivīpāla mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ diṣṭam etat purā nūnam evaṃbhāvi narādhipa
english: Hear it, protector of the earth, and set not your mind on grief; this was surely ordained of old to come to pass thus, lord of men.

sanskrit: namaskṛtvā pitus te 'haṃ pārāśaryāya dhīmate yasya prasādād divyaṃ me prāptaṃ jñānam anuttamam
english: Having made obeisance to your father, the wise son of Parāśara, by whose grace I have obtained the divine and unsurpassed knowledge —
